# pcd_blockstorage_volume_transfer (Resource)

Offers a Cinder volume for transfer to another project. Creating this resource creates the offer and records its `auth_key`; a configuration that authenticates in the receiving project accepts it with `pcd_blockstorage_volume_transfer_accept`, which moves the volume, and every snapshot of it, into that project. Destroying this resource before the offer is accepted cancels the offer.

The volume must be `available` (not attached), and so must each of its snapshots. While the offer is pending the volume's status is `awaiting-transfer`, and Cinder refuses to attach, extend or retype it. Encrypted volumes cannot be transferred.

Anyone who has the transfer ID and `auth_key` can accept the volume into a project they belong to until the offer is accepted or canceled. The key is stored in the Terraform state in plain text, so protect the state accordingly.

A transfer moves a volume between projects. Accepting an offer in the project that made it is not supported: Cinder then reports the transfer exactly like a canceled one, and this resource leaves the state.

**After the offer is accepted**, the offering configuration still declares a volume that now belongs to another project. A project member can no longer read it, so Terraform drops the volume from state and plans a new, empty volume, and, because this resource refers to the volume, a new offer for it. An admin still reads it, so the configuration keeps managing it, and a destroy deletes it from its new project. Either way, replace the blocks of the volume, of this resource and of any `pcd_blockstorage_snapshot` of the volume with `removed` blocks that keep the objects (Terraform 1.7 or later; use `terraform state rm` before that), and import the volume where it now belongs. The examples here and on the `pcd_blockstorage_volume_transfer_accept` page show both sides.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Offer a volume from the project this configuration signs in to.
resource "pcd_blockstorage_volume" "example" {
  name = "app-data"
  size = 10
}

resource "pcd_blockstorage_volume_transfer" "example" {
  volume_id = pcd_blockstorage_volume.example.id
  name      = "app-data to team-b"
}

# The receiving project needs both values, for example through remote state
# or a secret store.
output "transfer_id" {
  value = pcd_blockstorage_volume_transfer.example.id
}

output "transfer_auth_key" {
  value     = pcd_blockstorage_volume_transfer.example.auth_key
  sensitive = true
}

# Once the receiving project has accepted the offer, the volume, this offer
# and any pcd_blockstorage_snapshot of the volume belong to that project.
# Replace their resource blocks above with removed blocks, so Terraform
# forgets them without destroying anything (Terraform 1.7 or later):
#
# removed {
#   from = pcd_blockstorage_volume.example
#   lifecycle {
#     destroy = false
#   }
# }
#
# removed {
#   from = pcd_blockstorage_volume_transfer.example
#   lifecycle {
#     destroy = false
#   }
# }
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `volume_id` (String) The volume to offer. Changing this forces a new offer.

### Optional

- `name` (String) A name for the offer, not empty and without leading or trailing whitespace. Changing this forces a new offer: Cinder cannot change a transfer.
- `region` (String) The region. Defaults to the provider's region. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `accepted` (Boolean) Whether the offer was accepted. Cinder stops reporting a transfer once it is accepted or canceled, so the provider decides from the volume: it was accepted when the volume is no longer visible or belongs to another project, and canceled when the volume is still in the source project (the resource then leaves the state). An offer canceled outside Terraform whose volume was then deleted also reads as accepted.
- `auth_key` (String, Sensitive) The secret that accepts the offer. Cinder returns it only when the offer is created, so it is null after an import.
- `id` (String) The transfer ID. The receiving project needs it, with `auth_key`, to accept the offer.
- `source_project_id` (String) The project the volume belonged to when it was offered.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax. The IDs are assigned by PCD; the
[Importing guide](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/platform9/pcd/latest/docs/guides/importing)
explains how to look them up.

```shell
# Find the transfer ID with: pcdctl volume transfer request list
# Cinder returns auth_key only when the offer is created, so it stays empty after an import.
terraform import pcd_blockstorage_volume_transfer.example <transfer_id>
```
